it.a: Not all of it. Coding is a big part, but you also learn networks, databases, security, and how to work in a team. Some days are mostly thinking and planning.
For many people it is debugging, when something fails and you have to find out why. It can be frustrating, but it gets easier with practice.

it.q: Do I need to be good at math?
it.a: Some areas use math, like data and algorithms, and others use much less. Logical thinking helps more than speed with numbers.
Many become software developers, but others work in networks, security, data, or technical support. The range is wide.
More than people expect. Big projects are built by teams, so planning, sharing work, and explaining your ideas matter a lot.

law.a: There is reading and remembering, but the main skill is applying rules to a situation and explaining your reasoning.

law.q: Do I have to speak in court?
law.a: Not every graduate does. Some argue in court, while others advise companies, draft documents, or work in government. Moot court lets you practise speaking.
A lot. Cases, statutes, and articles are part of almost every week, so reading carefully and efficiently becomes a key habit.
Many students find it hard to think precisely, because one word can change the meaning. It takes time to get used to.
Careers include law firms, company legal teams, government, and non-profit work. Not everyone becomes a courtroom lawyer.

english-ed.a: You study the language, but also how people learn it and how to teach it, including lesson planning and classroom management.

english-ed.q: Do I need to be fluent already?
english-ed.a: Good English helps, and you keep improving during the program. You do not need to be perfect on day one.

english-ed.q: How much teaching practice is there?
english-ed.a: You practise in microteaching with classmates, and later you spend time assisting in real classrooms.
Many students say keeping a class interested and managing the time in a lesson. Practice and feedback help.
Most teach in schools or language centers. Others work in training, writing learning materials, or education programs.
